correctness.rationale: The exact sketch update is a Euclidean rank-one orthogonal projection after y=H^{1/2}x. In dimension two, two-step zero error for any fixed nonzero start is almost surely equivalent to perpendicular sketch directions. Gaussian polar integration yields density sqrt(kappa)/(2pi(cos²+kappa sin²)). Maximal equality-coupling probability of its quarter-turn is the overlap integral, exactly 4/pi atan(kappa^-1/2). An explicit maximal coupling of full angles and independent conditional radial Rayleigh factors realizes exactly N(0,I) in each original sketch. For jointly Gaussian pairs the conditional regression s2=Cs1+Z gives zero success when Z has nonzero covariance; when Z=0, orthogonality would force C orthogonal and HC skew, possible only for scalar H. Independent pair repetition yields the exact geometric stopping law, including the isotropic endpoint. The package verifier checked 64000 examples and quadrature, not the general proof.

originality.rationale: The output is a condition-number-exact finite-termination frontier for a fixed Gaussian marginal and a separate jointly Gaussian no-go theorem. Inspected original RSN and stronger sketch-and-project bounds concern projected rates, not optimizing exact termination over temporal couplings. Published orthogonal-Gaussian-marginal features cover the isotropic construction only. The known maximal-coupling inequality is used, not claimed as new; the angular-density overlap integral and its Newton meaning, exact radial Gaussian lift, and Gaussian-class rigidity are the additional claimed contribution. Related indexed findings on iid planar sketch BFGS rates, stationary Haar-coupled Lanczos MSE and fixed sparse sketch distributions do not imply this event under the same law. Unindexed equivalent work cannot be excluded.
residual_risks: An equivalent anisotropic ACG/angular maximal-coupling calculation may exist in unindexed work.
The maximal-coupling inequality itself is classical; novelty attaches to its exact RSN specialization plus the joint-Gaussian impossibility.
No claim of priority over general optimal transport or over isotropic orthogonal Gaussian-row constructions.

value.rationale: The sharp exact two-step success probability and its geometric work distribution are intrinsic algorithmic quantities, not an arbitrary finite table. Fixing the full one-step Gaussian marginals while varying only dependence creates a qualitative change from never finite termination under joint Gaussian dependence (nonisotropic case) to almost-sure finite termination with optimal nonlinear block coupling. The exact dependence on Hessian conditioning provides a mathematically meaningful reproducibility benchmark. General sketch cost and implementation efficacy are not inferred.
